instructions.question: Does the tweet carry an upbeat evaluation, a critical or unhappy one, or no evaluation at all?
instructions.rule: Look for evaluative wording. Upbeat words, excited exclamations or emoticons (good, best, fun, omg, :), <3) with no complaint make it positive, even in promotions or plans. Critical judgments, setbacks, disappointment (:(, bummed), annoyance, sarcastic attacks or harmful news make it negative. Neutral covers tweets without evaluation: logistics, bare 'who's going?' invitations, plain questions, stats, dry headlines, court news, jokes attacking no one. Also neutral: pure tactical sports second-guessing, game recaps, and hassles laughed off ('lmao').

neutral.what: No evaluation: logistics, plain questions or invitations, stats, dry news, harmless jokes, tactical sports talk, laughed-off hassles.
examples: So .... Who's up for seeing Ant-Man with me on Saturday? 2:30pm showing. Let me know!
David Price should not have been pitching in the 8th. They can't get a 6-outs from the bullpen? Yankees - Jays
I could be going to digi tomorrow but I thought I was supposed to be seeing the girls but they cancelled lmao
neutral.cues: who's going, anyone wanna, should have started, dates, times, reports, scores, lmao
neutral.not_for: Praise or warmth makes it positive; an insult, harsh judgment, :( or real frustration makes it negative.

positive.what: Upbeat feeling or praise: excitement, affection, hope, warm promotions, fun plans, good news or achievements.
examples: Jason Aldean&Kenny Chesney tickets for sale. Concert is the 29th. Good seats for a really good price. Text me asap for more info!!
We always mess up when we get the chance to go up the table when Atleti or Barca mess up. PLEASE WIN TOMORROW :) @user
positive.cues: good, best, fun, can't wait, love, omggg, see you there, :), <3, Happy [day]
positive.not_for: Bare event listings, 'who's going with me?' and dry score lines are neutral.

negative.what: Criticism, contempt, complaints, disappointment, setbacks, sarcastic attacks, sadness, or news of violence or harm.
examples: "Caitlyn Jenner may not be ""down"" with gay marriage, but she should really understand that people are gonna see that as hypocritical."
I'm slightly bummed the Foo Fighters are playing Friday night of ACL rather than Sunday. I'm pretty much not gonna care the other 2 days.
A Thursday night with no Waterloo road on! #boring
negative.cues: hypocritical, bitter, racist, you just hate, bummed, dang it, :(, argh, #boring, attack
negative.not_for: Strong words used in excitement are positive.
